# System Migration Plan: Project Atlas
## Version 2.1 | Last Updated: 2026-03-01
## Migration Lead: David Chen | Sponsor: CTO Sandra Williams

### Executive Summary
Project Atlas is the comprehensive migration of our data infrastructure from the legacy on-premises data center (Facility A, Phoenix AZ) to AWS cloud. This migration covers 3 primary databases, 12 application services, and associated networking infrastructure.

### Critical Dates
- Migration Start: March 1, 2026
- Database Pre-staging: March 1-10
- Application Migration Window: March 10-14
- **Cutover Date: March 15, 2026 (Saturday, 02:00 UTC)**
- Post-Migration Validation: March 15-17
- Legacy Decommission: April 1, 2026
- Rollback Decision Point: March 15, 08:00 UTC (6 hours after cutover start)

### Migration Scope
1. **Databases** (see db-inventory.md for details)
   - PostgreSQL primary (product data, user data, orders)
   - MongoDB (analytics, event logs)
   - Redis cluster (session cache, rate limiting)

2. **Application Services**
   - api-gateway, user-service, catalog-service, order-service
   - notification-service, search-service, payment-service
   - admin-portal, reporting-service, scheduler-service
   - auth-service, file-service

3. **Infrastructure**
   - DNS cutover from on-prem to AWS Route53
   - SSL certificate migration to AWS Certificate Manager
   - VPN tunnels for hybrid connectivity during transition

### Success Criteria
- All services operational on AWS within 6-hour maintenance window
- Data integrity verified (checksums match pre/post migration)
- Latency within 10% of baseline for all critical paths
- Zero data loss
- Rollback executed successfully if needed within 6-hour window

### Stakeholder Communication
- Engineering: Daily standups during migration week
- Executive team: Daily status emails March 10-17
- Customers: Maintenance notification 7 days in advance
- Partners: API migration guide sent 30 days in advance

### Budget
- Migration tooling: $45,000
- AWS infrastructure (first 3 months): $72,000
- Consulting (DBA support): $30,000
- Contingency: $20,000
- Total: $167,000

# Database Inventory & Migration Plan
## Project Atlas - Database Details

### Database 1: PostgreSQL (Primary)
- **Current Location**: On-prem, Facility A, Server rack DB-01
- **Version**: PostgreSQL 14.8
- **Size**: 2.4 TB (as of March 1, 2026)
- **Growth Rate**: ~15 GB/week
- **Tables**: 847 tables across 12 schemas
- **Critical Tables**: users (45M rows), products (8M rows), orders (120M rows), order_items (380M rows)
- **Migration Method**: AWS DMS (Database Migration Service) with continuous replication
- **Pre-staging**: Initial bulk load March 1-5, continuous replication March 5-15
- **Estimated Migration Time**: 18 hours for initial bulk load, then real-time sync
- **Target**: AWS RDS PostgreSQL 14.8, db.r6g.4xlarge (Multi-AZ)
- **Special Considerations**:
  - Custom extensions: pg_trgm, PostGIS, pg_stat_statements
  - Requires careful handling of sequences and auto-increment values
  - Foreign key constraints must be disabled during bulk load, re-enabled after
  - Connection string changes affect all 12 application services

### Database 2: MongoDB (Analytics)
- **Current Location**: On-prem, Facility A, Server rack DB-02
- **Version**: MongoDB 6.0
- **Size**: 800 GB
- **Collections**: 34 collections
- **Critical Collections**: events (2.1B documents), user_analytics (45M documents), page_views (890M documents)
- **Migration Method**: mongodump/mongorestore + oplog tailing for sync
- **Pre-staging**: Initial dump March 3-5, oplog sync March 5-15
- **Estimated Migration Time**: 8 hours for initial restore
- **Target**: AWS DocumentDB 6.0 compatible, db.r6g.2xlarge
- **Special Considerations**:
  - Some MongoDB-specific features not supported in DocumentDB (need testing)
  - Aggregation pipelines may need optimization for DocumentDB
  - TTL indexes must be verified post-migration
  - Sharding configuration needs to be adapted

### Database 3: Redis Cluster (Cache)
- **Current Location**: On-prem, Facility A, Server rack CACHE-01
- **Version**: Redis 7.0
- **Size**: 50 GB across 6 nodes
- **Key Patterns**: session:*, ratelimit:*, cache:product:*, cache:user:*
- **Migration Method**: Cold migration (cache will be rebuilt)
- **Pre-staging**: None required (ephemeral data)
- **Estimated Migration Time**: 15 minutes (deploy new cluster, warm cache)
- **Target**: AWS ElastiCache Redis 7.0, cache.r6g.xlarge, 6-node cluster
- **Special Considerations**:
  - Sessions will be invalidated (users will need to re-login)
  - Rate limit counters will reset
  - Cache warming strategy needed to avoid thundering herd on PostgreSQL
  - Lua scripts must be tested on ElastiCache

### Data Integrity Verification
- Row counts compared pre/post for all PostgreSQL tables
- Document counts compared pre/post for MongoDB collections
- Checksum verification on critical tables (users, orders)
- Application-level smoke tests for data reads

### Backup Strategy During Migration
- PostgreSQL: WAL archiving to S3 every 5 minutes
- MongoDB: Continuous oplog backup
- Pre-migration full backup stored for 30 days
- Point-in-time recovery available for 7 days post-migration

# Rollback Plan
## Project Atlas - Contingency Procedures

### Rollback Decision Criteria
Rollback should be initiated if ANY of the following occur within the 6-hour window:
1. Data integrity check fails (checksum mismatch)
2. More than 2 critical services fail to start on AWS
3. Latency exceeds 200% of baseline for any critical path
4. Data loss is detected
5. Rollback decision point reached (08:00 UTC) without all services healthy

### Rollback Authority
- Migration Lead (David Chen) can initiate rollback
- CTO (Sandra Williams) must approve rollback after 04:00 UTC
- On-call DBA must confirm database rollback feasibility

### Rollback Procedures

#### Step 1: Stop Traffic to AWS (5 minutes)
- Update Route53 to point back to on-prem load balancer
- TTL is set to 60 seconds, so propagation is fast
- Verify DNS propagation using multiple resolvers

#### Step 2: Stop Application Services on AWS (10 minutes)
- Scale all ECS services to 0 tasks
- This prevents any writes to AWS databases during rollback

#### Step 3: Database Rollback (varies by database)

**PostgreSQL (30-60 minutes)**:
- Stop DMS replication task
- Verify on-prem PostgreSQL is still running and accepting connections
- Check for any writes that went to AWS RDS during cutover
- If writes occurred on AWS: run delta sync script to replay to on-prem
- Verify data integrity on on-prem database
- Re-enable on-prem connection pools

**MongoDB (20-30 minutes)**:
- Stop oplog tailing process
- Verify on-prem MongoDB cluster health
- Run document count verification
- Re-point application config to on-prem MongoDB

**Redis (5 minutes)**:
- No rollback needed - on-prem Redis cluster remains running during migration
- Sessions on on-prem are still valid
- Cache will rebuild naturally

#### Step 4: Restart On-Prem Services (15 minutes)
- Scale up on-prem application instances
- Verify all services are healthy
- Run smoke test suite

#### Step 5: Verification (30 minutes)
- Monitor error rates for 30 minutes
- Verify all API endpoints responding correctly
- Check database connection counts are normal
- Confirm customer-facing functionality works

#### Step 6: Communication (immediate)
- Notify engineering team via Slack #migration channel
- Send executive status update
- If customer-facing impact: send customer notification
- Schedule post-rollback review for next business day

### Total Estimated Rollback Time: 90-120 minutes

### Post-Rollback Actions
- Root cause analysis within 24 hours
- Remediation plan within 48 hours
- Revised migration schedule within 1 week
- All migration infrastructure kept running for retry

# Network Migration Plan
## Project Atlas - Network Infrastructure Changes

### Current State (On-Prem)
- Public IP range: 203.0.113.0/24
- Internal network: 10.0.0.0/16
- Load balancer: F5 BIG-IP (on-prem)
- DNS: Self-hosted BIND servers
- SSL: Certificates managed manually, stored in HashiCorp Vault
- Firewall: Palo Alto PA-5200 series

### Target State (AWS)
- VPC CIDR: 172.16.0.0/16
- Public subnets: 172.16.1.0/24, 172.16.2.0/24 (us-east-1a, us-east-1b)
- Private subnets: 172.16.10.0/24, 172.16.11.0/24 (us-east-1a, us-east-1b)
- Load balancer: AWS ALB (Application Load Balancer)
- DNS: AWS Route53
- SSL: AWS Certificate Manager (auto-renewal)
- Firewall: AWS Security Groups + WAF

### Migration Steps

#### Phase 1: Hybrid Connectivity (March 1-10)
1. Establish AWS Direct Connect (already provisioned, 1 Gbps)
2. Set up site-to-site VPN as backup
3. Configure VPC peering for cross-region communication
4. Verify latency between on-prem and AWS < 5ms
5. Test database replication throughput over Direct Connect

#### Phase 2: DNS Preparation (March 10-14)
1. Migrate DNS zones to Route53 (read-only, shadowing BIND)
2. Set TTL on all critical records to 60 seconds (down from 3600)
3. Prepare Route53 health checks for all services
4. Test DNS failover scenarios
5. Verify all internal service discovery records

#### Phase 3: Cutover (March 15)
1. Update Route53 records to point to AWS ALB
2. Keep on-prem F5 running as fallback
3. Monitor DNS propagation globally
4. Verify SSL termination on ALB
5. Confirm WAF rules are active

#### Phase 4: Post-Cutover (March 15-31)
1. Monitor traffic distribution (expect some stragglers due to DNS caching)
2. Gradually reduce on-prem capacity
3. Keep VPN tunnel active for 30 days
4. Decommission Direct Connect after 60 days

### IP Address Changes
| Service | Old IP | New IP (ALB) |
|---------|--------|-------------|
| api.company.com | 203.0.113.10 | ALB (dynamic, DNS-based) |
| admin.company.com | 203.0.113.11 | ALB (dynamic, DNS-based) |
| webhooks.company.com | 203.0.113.15 | ALB (dynamic, DNS-based) |

### Firewall Rules
- All on-prem rules replicated as AWS Security Group rules
- WAF rules ported from Palo Alto to AWS WAF
- Rate limiting moved from F5 to application-level (Redis-backed)

### Risks
- Direct Connect failure during migration (mitigated by VPN backup)
- DNS propagation delays affecting some customers
- IP-based whitelisting by partners needs coordination (3 partners identified)

# Migration Testing Checklist
## Project Atlas - Pre and Post Migration Verification

### Pre-Migration Tests (Run March 14)

#### Database Verification
- [ ] PostgreSQL row counts recorded for all critical tables
- [ ] MongoDB document counts recorded for all collections
- [ ] PostgreSQL checksum computed for users, orders tables
- [ ] Backup verification: restore test on isolated environment
- [ ] DMS replication lag < 1 second
- [ ] MongoDB oplog tailing caught up to real-time

#### Application Readiness
- [ ] All 12 services deployed and tested on AWS (staging config)
- [ ] Connection strings updated in AWS Parameter Store
- [ ] Environment variables verified for each service
- [ ] Health check endpoints responding on all services
- [ ] Feature flags set for migration mode

#### Network Readiness
- [ ] Route53 zones verified against current BIND zones
- [ ] TTL lowered to 60 seconds on all critical records
- [ ] Direct Connect throughput tested (> 500 Mbps sustained)
- [ ] VPN failover tested
- [ ] SSL certificates provisioned on ALB

### Post-Migration Tests (Run within 30 minutes of cutover)

#### Smoke Tests
- [ ] User login flow (web and mobile)
- [ ] Product search returns results
- [ ] Order placement end-to-end
- [ ] Payment processing (test transaction)
- [ ] Email notification delivery
- [ ] Admin portal accessible
- [ ] API endpoints responding (sample of 20 critical endpoints)
- [ ] WebSocket connections establish successfully

#### Data Integrity
- [ ] PostgreSQL row counts match pre-migration
- [ ] MongoDB document counts match pre-migration
- [ ] PostgreSQL checksums match for users, orders tables
- [ ] Sample data spot-check: 100 random users, 100 random orders
- [ ] Sequence values are correct (no gaps or resets)
- [ ] Timestamps are in correct timezone

#### Performance
- [ ] API latency within 10% of baseline (p50 and p99)
- [ ] Database query latency within 15% of baseline
- [ ] Redis cache hit rate > 80% within first hour
- [ ] No memory leaks detected in first 2 hours
- [ ] CPU utilization stable and within expected range

#### Monitoring
- [ ] All Datadog dashboards showing data
- [ ] PagerDuty alerts configured for AWS services
- [ ] CloudWatch alarms active
- [ ] Log aggregation working (CloudWatch Logs -> Datadog)
- [ ] Error rate below 0.5% threshold

### Rollback Test (Run March 13)
- [ ] Simulate rollback procedure in staging environment
- [ ] Verify rollback completes within 120 minutes
- [ ] Verify data integrity after rollback
- [ ] Document any issues found and update rollback plan

### Sign-Off Required
- [ ] Migration Lead (David Chen)
- [ ] DBA (Priya Patel)
- [ ] DevOps Lead (Alex Rivera)
- [ ] QA Lead (Tom Nguyen)
- [ ] CTO (Sandra Williams) - final go/no-go
